summary: This program defines a function that sends Beepo the robot waiter to a table and greets the customers there, then calls it three times with three different table numbers.

lines.text: The `def` keyword defines the function, and `table_number` is its parameter \u2014 a placeholder that stands in for whichever table number is supplied when the function is called.

lines.code: """Beepo the robot waiter greets at the specified table."""
lines.text: A docstring is a short description placed as the first line inside a function, explaining in plain words what the function is for so anyone reading the code later knows its purpose.

lines.code: print(f"Beep boop! Rolling up to table {table_number}...")
lines.text: The body of the function is indented, and everything indented under `def` belongs to the function. The f-string drops the current value of `table_number` into the message, so the wording changes with each call.
Defining a function does nothing on its own; this call is what actually runs the body. The `1` is the argument, and it becomes the value of `table_number` for the duration of this call.
Three calls with three different arguments reuse the same four lines of logic, which is the point of a function \u2014 Beepo visits a different table each time without you rewriting the greeting.
